purpose: Scores early ischaemic change in the middle cerebral artery territory on non-contrast CT in hyperacute ischaemic stroke, as part of the pre-treatment CT assessment before thrombolysis.
exam: non-contrast CT head for suspected acute ischaemic stroke
system: Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) for early ischaemic change in the MCA territory on non-contrast CT
aliases: Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score
Alberta Stroke Programme Early CT Score

summary.text: ASPECTS scores early ischaemic change in the middle-cerebral-artery territory on two axial non-contrast CT levels: 10 points, minus one for each of ten regions showing it.

locator.section: Methods, Procedures: ASPECTS allots the middle-cerebral-artery territory 10 points; one point is subtracted for early ischaemic change in each defined region; a normal CT scores 10 and 0 indicates diffuse ischaemia throughout the territory (journal p1671)

summary.text: A score of 10 means no early ischaemic change in the ten scored regions; 0 means change throughout the MCA territory. Lower scores mean more extensive early change.

locator.section: Methods, Procedures: ASPECTS allots the middle-cerebral-artery territory 10 points; one point is subtracted for early ischaemic change in each defined region; a normal CT scores 10 and 0 indicates diffuse ischaemia throughout the territory (journal p1671)

summary.text: Cohort: 156 patients treated with intravenous alteplase alone within 3 hours of stroke onset at two North American hospitals, March 1996 to May 1999; non-contrast CT on 10 mm slices. These are the only figures below; they are not a general prognosis and not for thrombectomy selection.

locator.section: Methods, Patients and Procedures; Results (journal p1671-1672)

summary.text: In that cohort a baseline score of 7 or less was associated with dependence or death at 3 months and with more symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage than a score above 7 (scores 8 to 10 together).

locator.section: Statistics (journal p1671-1672): a score of 7 or less versus more than 7 discriminated independence from dependence and death; Results (journal p1672)

definitions.text: Subcortical structures score 3 points: caudate, lentiform nucleus and internal capsule.

definitions.text: Early ischaemic change means focal brain swelling or parenchymal hypoattenuation; hypoattenuation is abnormally low attenuation relative to other parts of the same structure or the contralateral hemisphere.

locator.section: Methods, Procedures (journal p1671)

definitions.text: The score is read from two standard axial CT cuts: one at the level of the thalamus and basal ganglia, and one just rostral to the ganglionic structures.

pitfalls.text: Cohort: 156 patients treated with intravenous alteplase alone within 3 hours of stroke onset at two North American hospitals, March 1996 to May 1999; non-contrast CT on 10 mm slices. It predates thrombectomy; the figures are not for patients considered for thrombectomy or any other treatment.

locator.section: Methods, Procedures; Results (journal p1671-1672)

pitfalls.text: ASPECTS was derived and tested in anterior-circulation (MCA territory) ischaemia; 23 posterior-circulation patients were not analysed. It is not pc-ASPECTS, which is a different posterior-circulation score not covered by this source.

locator.section: Methods, Patients: only patients thought to have anterior-circulation ischaemia were included in the analysis (journal p1670-1671); Results: 23 patients with posterior-circulation ischaemia were not analysed (p1672)

pitfalls.text: A score of 10 means no early ischaemic change in the ten MCA regions only; it does not exclude haemorrhage, an old infarct, or ischaemia outside the MCA territory.

locator.section: Methods, Procedures: ASPECTS allots the middle-cerebral-artery territory 10 points; one point is subtracted for early ischaemic change in each defined region; a normal CT scores 10 and 0 indicates diffuse ischaemia throughout the territory (journal p1671)

pitfalls.text: The odds ratio of 14 for symptomatic haemorrhage rests on 10 events in total (95% CI 1.8 to 117; the text gives 2 to 117). The 1% rate above 7 is 1 of 91, slightly above the 0.6% on placebo in the NINDS trial.

locator.section: Discussion (journal p1673)

pitfalls.text: The cut-off of 7 or less versus above 7 was suggested by a review of the study data, not set in advance.

locator.section: Statistics (journal p1671)

pitfalls.text: Study limitation: it could not show how patients scoring 7 or less would have fared without treatment, and the authors called for validation in a randomised controlled study.

pitfalls.text: ASPECTS is scored in whole points from 0 to 10; the source defines no fractional score.
